content:
Next month's 26th marks the one-year anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit its report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports indicated that the government has activated the Head of Department Accountability System to investigate the administrative responsibility for the fire and has reassigned political assistants to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (the 6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism had been activated, stating that the government has made a series of arrangements and will promptly implement reforms and pursue accountability after the report is submitted. The luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley was revealed to have reinforcing steel that did not match the plans. Lee stated that the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With multiple engineering projects being exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches importance to the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, which concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

It is nearly a year since the Wang Fuk Court fire, and the independent committee is expected to submit its report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports said two political assistants — former Deputy Secretary for Security Victor Mok and Commissioner for Sports Choy Kin-bun — would provide support to an investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically responsible for preparatory work on administrative accountability.

Before attending the Executive Council meeting today, Chief Executive John Lee met the press and was asked whether the reports were true. He was also asked whether the activation of the Head of Department Accountability System to investigate responsibility means that even with a report, if official accountability is involved, there will not be immediate results — how long would the public have to wait?

Lee said he had made it clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he would actively study and follow up on its recommendations, carry out reforms and announce the details. He did not give a direct answer on whether political assistants have already been reassigned to prepare for the preliminary investigation work, saying only that "the government has made a series of arrangements during this period", and stressed that after the report is submitted, based on its content, he would "implement comprehensive reforms as soon as possible in the short term and pursue accountability", with detailed announcements to follow.

Lee said that after the independent committee submits its report, he will implement reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible based on the report's content. (File photo)

Lee reiterated once again that improvement measures are urgent, and so when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced seven priority improvement measures, including banning smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, strengthening disciplinary and punitive actions against professionals and contractors, improving compliance in owners' corporations, studying the criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, establishing prequalification lists for consultants and contractors, and researching solutions to better assist the public with professional aspects of construction projects.

According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on civil service appointments, promotions and disciplinary matters. The Head of Department Accountability System was introduced by Chief Executive John Lee in last year's Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism based on the severity of departmental issues. If the problem is less serious in nature or is an isolated incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the head of department. If the department has a serious problem, or it involves extensive or repetitive systemic issues, or may involve the role of the head of department, a second-tier investigation will be launched by an investigation小组 led by the Public Service Commission.

The luxury residence One Stanley was revealed to have units where the reinforcing steel did not match the plans. Lee said he would not comment on cases still under investigation, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley "steel pulling" — Development Bureau requested to monitor investigation

Recently, construction projects have been exposed for problems one after another, including lift shaft tilting at the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples at a Tung Chung public housing estate not meeting strength standards, and floor slab reinforcing steel at the luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley not matching the plans. Lee was asked whether there are problems with construction and even project supervision.

Responding to the One Stanley project issue, he said the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "to ascertain whether construction quality and site supervision were adequate, and will handle it strictly in accordance with the law". As the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the case investigation. He stressed that he attaches importance to the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, "and is concerned about whether professionals related to the project have performed their supervisory duties diligently, and whether contractors have carried out construction in violation of regulations". He also said it concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will definitely enforce the law strictly.

He has also requested the Development Bureau to enhance regulatory requirements and penalties in legal aspects for construction projects overall, to ensure the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punish relevant personnel in violation, and safeguard the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction projects. The Development Bureau will submit amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen regulation, enhance the disciplinary system and penalties, and the authorities will press ahead with the work at full speed.

The difficulty faced by nursing graduates in finding jobs has recently drawn attention. Lee said demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has over 3,000 nursing vacancies that graduates can apply for. (File photo)

ExCo member Tommy Cheung criticises "unions putting on an act" — Lee says demand exists long-term

Discussion of nurses' difficulty in finding jobs has heated up recently. The source was a radio Phone-in programme after the Policy Address, in which a Mr Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in a disciplinary force, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and that his daughter, a nursing graduate, became unemployed immediately after graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority's introduction of Mainland healthcare personnel. Executive Council member Tommy Cheung subsequently questioned whether it was the unions "calling in pretending to be people", and stated he would fully support importing talent from outside.

Reporters asked about the difficulty nursing graduates face in finding jobs, how to solve the problem of vacancies being concentrated in experienced nurses, and how to respond to ExCo members' remarks being accused of intensifying social contradictions. Lee said that in every industry, there are cases of graduates not seeking employment immediately after graduation for individual reasons, or of recruiting organisations selecting those most suitable for their needs, "resulting in some individuals not being hired". He stressed that society's demand for nurses has always existed, especially with Hong Kong's healthcare continuously developing and the population ageing trend, "so recruitment numbers will ultimately inevitably reflect this existing demand". He also said without naming anyone, "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, which can help everyone discuss the issue more clearly".

Lee also said that according to 2025/26 figures, there are about 4,000 potential nursing graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 applied for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has over 3,000 nursing vacancies, "nursing graduates can apply, and have a chance of being hired".

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier在接受 multiple media interviews clarified that the government's recruitment policy definitely prioritises local talent. Lee also reiterated that according to the Hospital Authority's current number of nurses, "99.8% are locally trained nurses in Hong Kong", clearly implementing the policy of prioritising local talent in hiring. He also pointed out that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, with the remaining 60% in other healthcare positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, and private medical institutions. He stressed that society's demand for nurses exists long-term, and the government will, in line with healthcare service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia, and do a good job in planning for healthcare training and manpower development.
